## The hotspot picture

Every `high_fan_in_fan_out` finding, with the size findings that land on the same file:

| File | fan-in | fan-out | God File | Biggest God Function | test_gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/utils.ts` | **18** | 1 | 424 lines (1.4×) | — | 0 |
| `src/plugin.ts` | **10** | 3 | — | `buildFinished` 103 (1.7×) | 0.75 |
| `src/log.ts` | 9 | 0 | — | — | 0.75 |
| `test/utils.ts` | 9 | 0 | — | — | 0 |
| `src/index.ts` | 4 | **17** | 459 lines (1.5×) | `build` 293 (4.9×) | 0 |
| `src/esbuild/index.ts` | 1 | **11** | — | `runEsbuild` 237 (4.0×) | 0 |
| `src/rollup.ts` | 0 | 7 | — | `getRollupConfig` 122 (2.0×) | 0.75 |
| `src/api-extractor.ts` | 1 | 6 | — | `rollupDtsFiles` 85 (1.4×) | 0.75 |

The p95 cutoff is 9 importers / 6 imports; p99 is 10 / 11. So `utils.ts` (18) and `plugin.ts` (10) are the only files above the p99 fan-in line, and `index.ts` (17) and `esbuild/index.ts` (11) are the only ones above p99 fan-out.

Fan-in and fan-out are different problems and want different fixes: **fan-in is ripple** (who breaks when you change this), **fan-out is context load** (how much an agent must hold to change this safely). Only fan-in work actually reduces blast radius across the codebase; fan-out work reduces the odds of a wrong edit.

## Triage order

**1. `src/utils.ts` — do this first.**
Fan-in 18, the highest in the repo by 80%, and it's a 424-line God File (`blast_radius_importers: 29`). It's the only file that is simultaneously the most-imported module *and* over the size threshold. Two things make it the cheap win: it has **no** `large_function` findings, so the 424 lines are many small functions rather than one tangle — splitting by responsibility is a move-and-re-export, not a rewrite. And `test_gap: 0` means the existing suite covers it. Splitting `removeFiles` / `ensureTempDeclarationDir` / `jsoncParse` into concern-scoped modules means the next 18 importers pull in a narrow surface instead of the whole drawer. Fold in `crime_00054` (`jsoncParse` swallows its error and returns `{}` — 18 importers can't distinguish "no data" from "it broke") while you're in there.

**2. `src/plugin.ts` — second, but write tests before you touch it.**
Fan-in 10 puts it at the p99 line, and `buildFinished` (103 lines, `agent_risk 0.54` — the second-highest agent_risk in the whole scan) sits inside it. The distinguishing fact versus `utils.ts` is `test_gap: 0.75`: 10 importers depend on a file with a 103-line untested method. That inverts the sequence — characterization tests on `buildFinished` first, then extract helpers. This is the finding where an agent editing one section and missing another is most likely to ship a regression to 10 consumers.

**3. `src/esbuild/index.ts` — best reward-to-risk ratio in the list.**
Fan-out 11 (p99), and `runEsbuild` is 237 lines (4.0×) with a 38-property options bag (`crime_00040`). But fan-in is **1**. Refactoring it can only break one importer, so the risk of the change is near zero while the payoff — an agent no longer needing 11 modules plus a 38-field implicit contract in context to edit the esbuild path — is large. Do it before `index.ts` precisely because the blast radius of the *refactor itself* is one file.

**4. `src/index.ts` — extract functions, do not split the module.**
Fan-out 17 (highest in the repo), 459 lines, and four God Functions stacked inside each other: `build` 293, an anonymous 274, `mainTasks` 194, `normalizeOptions` 96. It's the worst file by raw numbers, but it's fourth because fan-in 4 means restructuring it buys little ripple reduction, and it's the package entry point — moving exports here is the one change that can break consumers outside the repo. Extract `normalizeOptions` and `mainTasks` into their own modules and leave the export surface identical. Note `crime_00034`: `build` is named like a pure transformation but calls `createLogger` and `removeFiles`, which is exactly the trap for an agent that reads the name and not the 293 lines.

## Leave alone

**`src/log.ts` — explicitly do not refactor.** Fan-in 9, fan-out **0**, no size finding, no God Function. That is what a healthy leaf utility looks like; the detector flags it on connectivity alone. Its only findings are two unprefixed booleans (`onlyImportant`, `silent`) — and renaming those touches 9 importers to reduce risk by nothing. The `treat_as_load_bearing` action is the right read here: high fan-in with zero fan-out and zero size problems means *stable*, not *dangerous*.

**`test/utils.ts`** — fan-in 9, but its 9 importers are test files. Blast radius is confined to the suite. The unbounded `Promise.all` fan-out (`crime_00069`) is real but bounded by fixture size in practice.

**`src/rollup.ts` — defer despite the high-severity finding.** `getRollupConfig` is 122 lines, high severity, and misleadingly named (`get*` prefix on a function calling `setSilent` and `removeFiles`). But fan-in is **0** and `blast_radius_importers: 0` — nothing ripples out of this file. It's a leaf. Worth fixing eventually for the naming lie; it does not belong in a blast-radius triage.

**`src/cli-main.ts`** — `main` at 153 lines (2.5×) is the third-largest function in the repo, but `blast_radius_importers: 2`. Big and isolated. Same logic: severity is high, blast radius isn't.

**`src/esbuild/postcss.ts`** — `postcssPlugin` 140 + `setup` 126, both high severity, plus return-shape inconsistency (3 shapes, 0% key overlap). Not a connectivity hotspot; `blast_radius: 0.14`. Queue behind the four above.

**`src/api-extractor.ts`** — fan-out 6 sits exactly *at* the p95 cutoff, not above it. Borderline by construction. Leave it.

## Two caveats on this ranking

`churn: 0` and `recency: 0` on every single finding — this fixture has no usable git history, so the ordering is purely structural. If real churn data existed it could easily promote a file I've deferred; a 122-line function nobody has touched in two years is a very different risk from one edited weekly.

And `test_gap: 0` is softer than it looks. There are 12 `weak_test_signal` findings, six of them tests with **zero** assertions (`test/index.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`, `test/tsconfig.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`). So the suite nominally covering `utils.ts` and `index.ts` is partly hollow. Before step 1, spot-check that the `utils.ts` coverage is real assertions and not one of the no-op tests — otherwise pick 1 inherits pick 2's "write characterization tests first" constraint.
